provenance.notes: video-derived via MediaPipe fallback + GMR (no SMPL-X); rep 1 of the drill: en garde 0.33-1.6 s (sword arm extends ~1.3-1.7 s), advance 1.6-2.2 s, lunge 2.2-2.8 s, held ~1.5 s, recovery 4.4-4.93 s; the drill flows straight from the recovery into a retreat back to the start, so the clip is cut as the front foot lands (4.93 s; the back foot is already sliding back ~15 cm) and the end hold is synthesized (eased to rest over 0.25 s, front foot put down by plant_still_feet). Ends FORWARD: root +1.1 m along +x (advance ~0.5 m + back-foot drag on the lunge). Source fencer is left-handed (sidecar), mirrored to R. Same as advance_lunge_v2 but with a 2 s end hold (v2: 0.5 s); v2's policy fell ~1.5 s into holding the final pose. v2 superseded advance_lunge_v1 (frames 10-146), whose end en garde floated 10-16 cm and whose front foot hovered 10-15 cm through the held lunge; cleaned with fixes.contact_floor_track edge fallback + fixes.plant_still_feet (front foot lowered up to 15 cm by leg IK). Caveats: pelvis yaw ~74 deg off the line; the recovery is fast (front foot ~3 m/s just before the eased end); warn; slip 1.2 cm, pen 1.0 cm, limits 0, max 15.3 rad/s, 7.07 s; v4 = advance_lunge_v3 with wrist pitch and yaw of both arms set to 0 (fixes.neutralize_wrists; max change 1.21 rad). Video pose has no wrist rotation, so those angles were a retargeting by-product; with the wrist motors' 0.075 rad action scale they needed actions up to 16 and were never tracked (left wrist error 0.2-0.27 rad in advance_lunge_cut_v3).
